server.title: Stream board server
server.description: Serves a clean, high-contrast draft board over local HTTP for use as an OBS browser source.
server.portHint: 1024–65535. Changing the port requires restarting the server and updating your OBS scene.
server.picksHint: The Picks View shows each player's hero and drafted abilities as two compact team strips for your in-game scene. Open the URL in a browser to tune them and generate the per-team OBS source links. It keeps showing the finished draft for the whole game, even after the overlay is closed.
server.autostart: Start the server when the app launches
server.errorPortInUse: That port is already in use — pick another port and start again.
server.errorGeneric: The server failed to start. Check the logs for details.
server.errorInvalidPort: Invalid port. Use a number between 1024 and 65535.

background.title: Background mode
background.description: Run the draft session without the overlay appearing on your screen. Scans, automatic tracking, the stream board and the Twitch extension all work exactly as usual.
background.hint: For streamers who broadcast the board or the Twitch extension but do not want the overlay while they play. Activate a session as normal — the hotkeys Ctrl+Shift+S and Ctrl+Shift+R still scan and rescan.
background.activeNote: A session is running in the background right now.
background.autoCloseNote: Overlay auto-close stays off in this mode: there is nothing covering the game, and closing would clear the draft mid-match.
background.resetDone: Draft cleared. The next scan starts a fresh draft.
background.controlsHint: A new match clears the previous draft automatically. Use Reset draft if a draft is left over, or End session to stop tracking.

gsi.title: Dota 2 Game State Integration
gsi.description: Lets Dota send player names, game phase, and clock to the stream board. Requires a one-time config file in your Dota folder and a Dota restart.
gsi.notDetected: Dota installation not found — pick the "dota 2 beta" folder manually.
gsi.cfgOutdated: Your installed config predates the caster stats (items are missing from it). Reinstall it and restart Dota 2 to enable them.
gsi.writeSuccess: Config written to {{path}}. Restart Dota 2 for it to take effect.
gsi.errorDotaNotFound: Could not locate the Dota 2 installation. Use Browse to pick the "dota 2 beta" folder.
gsi.errorWriteFailed: Failed to write the config file. Check the logs for details.
gsi.portMismatch: The installed config points at port {{cfgPort}}, but the stream server uses port {{streamPort}} — Dota can't reach the app. Reinstall the config file and restart Dota 2.
gsi.portNote: The config pins the current server port — reinstall it after changing the port.
gsi.spectatorNote: All 10 player names are only available while spectating/casting. When playing, Dota reports only your own name.

icons.title: Ability icons
icons.description: The board uses official ability icons, downloaded once and cached locally. Prefetch them now so the first draft renders instantly even without internet access.
icons.error: Prefetch failed. Check the logs for details.

obs.title: OBS setup
obs.step1: Start the server and copy the board URL.
obs.step2: In OBS: Sources → Add → Browser, paste the URL, set the size to 1920×1080.
obs.step3: The background is transparent by default. Append ?bg=dark for a solid background or ?bg=chroma for a green screen.
obs.note: The board follows your overlay scans: the pool appears after a scan (Ctrl+Shift+S) and picks update after each rescan (Ctrl+Shift+R).

twitch.title: Twitch extension
twitch.description: Lets your viewers click the abilities in your draft on Twitch. Pair the app with your channel once, then keep broadcasting on.
twitch.step1: Install the Ability Draft Plus extension on your Twitch channel and open its configuration page.
twitch.step2: Copy the pairing code shown there.
twitch.step3: Paste the code below and press Pair.
twitch.enableHint: Sends the draft board to your viewers after every scan. Game-phase tracking needs the stream server running; OBS is not required.
twitch.testSent: Update delivered to the extension backend.
twitch.errorInvalidCode: That pairing code is invalid or has expired — generate a new one on the extension's configuration page.
twitch.errorNetwork: Could not reach the extension backend. Check your internet connection.
twitch.errorUnauthorized: The channel pairing is no longer valid. Unpair and pair again.
twitch.errorPublishFailed: The last update could not be delivered. It will be retried automatically.
twitch.errorLiveFailed: Live game stats are not reaching viewers — the extension backend may be out of date. The draft board is unaffected.
twitch.errorTooLarge: The draft update was too large for Twitch and was not delivered.
twitch.errorVersion: The extension backend requires a newer app version. Please update the app.
twitch.errorNothingToSend: Nothing to send yet — scan a draft first.
